notes.text: For more than 8, cook the beef in 3 or 4 batches so the pan stays hot.

move.title: Thin slices, big flavor
move.body: Slice the beef thin, soak it in a sweet and salty marinade, and cook it fast in a very hot pan. Thin slices soak up flavor quickly and cook in a couple of minutes.

why.title: Why freeze it first
why.body: Raw beef is soft, so the knife slips and squishes it. Thirty minutes in the freezer firms it up just enough to cut thin, even slices.

why.title: Slice across the grain
why.body: Beef is made of long fibers lined up like a bundle of straws. Cutting across them leaves short fibers, so every bite is tender instead of chewy.

why.title: Why there's a pear in it
why.body: Pear adds sweetness, and its natural enzymes soften the outside of the meat while it marinates.

why.title: Why a very hot pan
why.body: A crowded or cool pan lets the juice pool, so the beef steams and turns gray. One layer in a hot pan browns it in seconds.

wrong.sign: The slices are thick and uneven
wrong.fix: Put the beef back in the freezer for 10 minutes, then try again with your sharpest knife.

wrong.sign: The beef is gray and sitting in liquid
wrong.fix: The pan is too crowded. Cook smaller batches and let the pan heat up again between them.
Serve it with more rice, and use a little less soy sauce next time.

quiz.q: Why do you slice across the grain?
choices: It makes each bite more tender
quiz.explain: Cutting across the fibers leaves them short, so the beef is easy to chew.

steps.text: Put the beef, still in its wrapper, in the freezer.
steps.tip: Make the marinade while it chills.

steps.text: Grate the pear on the large holes of the box grater, right into the big bowl. Grate the garlic and ginger on the small holes.
steps.tip: Stop when your fingers get close to the grater. Chop the last bit with a knife instead.

steps.text: Add the soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, black pepper, and green onions to the bowl. Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Unwrap the beef on the cutting board. Slice it across the grain as thin as you can, and drop the slices into the marinade.
steps.tip: Thinner than a pencil is perfect.

steps.text: Wash your hands, the knife, and the cutting board with hot, soapy water. Wipe the counter.
Stir with the wooden spoon so every slice is coated. Cover the bowl, put it in the fridge, and put the spoon in the sink.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the vegetable oil in the skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Use the tongs to lay about half the beef in the pan in one layer. Set the tongs down on a raw-meat spot, and don't use them for cooked beef.
Wash your hands. From here on, use the clean spatula for the beef in the pan.
Cook until the bottom is browned, about 2 minutes. Flip the slices with the spatula and cook 1 to 2 minutes more.
Fold a thick slice around the thermometer probe. It needs to read at least 145°F.
Move the cooked beef to the clean plate. Add the rest of the oil and cook the rest of the beef the same way, going back through the last four steps.
Turn off the stove. Let the beef rest for 3 minutes, then sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve over rice.
